items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: Start with the Neville brothers, Irma Thomas, Gene Knight, Oliver. And just ask them. They're going to tell you the same thing I'm saying.

ctx.x: Did you feel you were appreciated more by whites?

I'll tell you what. And you just ask. Start with the Neville brothers, Irma Thomas, Gene Knight, Oliver. And just ask them. They're going to tell you the same thing I'm saying. Hey, man, look. If there was a way. Well, I could. You know. Now, playing these social clubs is a different thing because you get set into playing a certain way. Okay. You know that people are going to come in there and sit down. You know the other people are going to sit down until they get half juice. And then they'll let loose. And we…
Because you don't work, you know, to black audiences, I'm saying, you were working to whites, did blacks ever tell you, you know, why don't you play for your own kind?

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-06-20
items.q: it was me, Jean Knight and Oliver Morgan, the three of us.

ctx.x: Cure. Anyway, and Bobby, Bobby a good buddy of mine. In fact, Bobby booked me on some gigs before Christmas. Some things I wouldn't have gotten. And the paying good and everything. But, um, I helped you know, I helped because really, and it was me, Jean Knight and Oliver Morgan, the three of us. Because we recognized what was going on and we used to talk about them. And you know. You cannot initiate it. I sure started on stage. I said, you know, they talk about the black musicians with the soul and all of this.…
Well, getting back, did you ever think of yourself as a rock and roll star? As a rock and roll artist? Yeah, yeah. You did?
